stem: Lakeshore Retail wants shoppers typing its storefront domain name to land on whichever of two Regional endpoints currently responds fastest, without shoppers ever having to change a URL.

choices.text: Insert a Gateway Load Balancer in front of both Regional endpoints
Publish two separate domain names, one per Region, for shoppers to choose
Configure Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing for the domain
Put a Network Load Balancer in front of both Regional endpoints

rationale: Route 53 latency-based routing resolves one domain name to whichever Region currently gives the shopper the best latency, with no URL change required. A Gateway Load Balancer inspects traffic through appliances, it does not choose between independent Regional endpoints by latency. Publishing two domain names forces shoppers to pick one themselves. A Network Load Balancer distributes connections within one deployment, it does not route DNS lookups between separate Regional endpoints.
